t: Look up at the Victoria Tower, the tallest part of the Palace of Westminster, at 98.5 metres. It stands at the south-west end, and is 2.2 metres taller than the Elizabeth Tower at the other end. Charles Barry and Augustus Pugin designed it in the Perpendicular Gothic style, and it was completed in 1860. Inside, it houses the Parliamentary Archives across twelve floors. A wrought-iron staircase of 553 steps once linked all fourteen floors, and five floors of it survive.
